source.title: Epistemology — Core Concepts
source.curatorExchanges: No additional dialogue or curator corrections outside the six original prompts in this source.

responseDecisions.1.1: Retain all thirty terms and their order. Correct certainty, intuition, deduction, fallibilism, contextualism and testimony definitions; distinguish internalist variants, source reliability and confidence. Retain eleven effective original entries verbatim.
responseDecisions.1.2: Retain thirty entries, including paired contrasts as source entries. Remove nonexistent image instruction and settled-Plato JTB attribution. Repair induction-as-fallacy, foundationalism-as-certainty, proposition/sentence, modality/necessity and sensation-as-uninterpreted conflations. Keep useful simple definitions.
responseDecisions.2.1: Keep ten concepts in order. Incorporate the previous edition’s useful bridge-report example within justification; distinguish copied reports from independent support. Explain regress, coherence-fiction challenge, truth/usefulness and contextualism versus subject stakes.
responseDecisions.2.2: Keep seven topics and nested source lists. Correct dismissal of friends’ testimony and anti-realism as total denial of reality. Add actual Gettier job/coins case; distinguish concepts learned through experience from a priori justification. No dialogue or curator correction existed here to reconstruct.
responseDecisions.3.1: Retain all selected figures and ordering. Correct Augustine’s period, Descartes founder claim, Locke sensation/reflection, Kant innate/a priori and Peirce usefulness caricatures; distinguish social epistemology from relativism. Explain methodological changes and continuity.
responseDecisions.3.2: Retain source figure/topic order while correcting period headings and explicitly identifying earlier antecedents. Correct Aristotle Hellenistic label, Augustine inventing skepticism, Kant nineteenth-century placement, Hume certainty caricature and linear rationalism-to-empiricism story. Add Gettier within analytic philosophy and explain verificationism’s difficulty.
responseDecisions.4.1: Keep nine fields. Date scope to the original conversation, avoid unsupported novelty ranking, add independent-source and AI-verification examples, qualify survey-based philosophical conclusions and consensus. Retain formal epistemology definition and closing connection.
responseDecisions.4.2: Keep six fields and three questions/aims each. Clarify plural feminist/decolonial positions, evidence requirements, embodied competence and description versus justification. Retain most original questions.
responseDecisions.5.1: Read all ten questions and the compact end key together. Replace father-of-empiricism ambiguity, overlapping hermeneutical-category answers and repetitive Locke question with precise targets including fallibilism. Add line breaks while retaining source paragraph layout and ten end answers.
responseDecisions.5.2: Read all ten questions and ten answers together. Repair skepticism wording, a priori meaning, gender generalization and overlapping testimony/social-epistemology and embodiment distractors. Preserve ordered question/key lists and exact counts.
responseDecisions.6.1: Retain twelve of fifteen discussion questions verbatim; revise JTB sufficiency and two historical questions to avoid assuming unestablished influence claims.
responseDecisions.6.2: Retain thirteen of fifteen questions verbatim; remove objective-versus-perspective false dichotomy and distinguish experiential report from further inferences.

research.scope: Complete short Gettier 1963 paper, including both cases and notes; UMass transcription. Initial Fitelson PDF timed out.
Locke Essay Book II chapter I opening on sensation/reflection and chapter VI passage on reflection; not the whole book.
Kant preface passage on objects/knowledge and introduction opening on experience versus a priori; edition dates checked. Not a whole Critique reading.
1878 essay passages on inquiry, truth and reality, especially final part; not a full Peirce corpus review.
Augustine City of God XI.26 argument against skeptical doubt about existing; not the whole work.
Fricker 2007 publisher book abstract and chapter abstracts for testimonial and hermeneutical injustice; no full-book access claimed.
Posterior Analytics II.19 on perception, memory, experience and primary premises; selected earlier demonstration passages. Not a complete Aristotle survey.
Enquiry editorial index paragraphs summarizing sections IV/V on induction and custom; no fresh full-text reading claimed for those sections.
Quine Epistemology Naturalized pages82–84 psychology/input-output passage; 1969 date corroborated against publisher chapter metadata. Not the whole chapter.

limitations: Only Epistemology — Core Concepts received full editorial review this run; ten current-batch pages remain pending. No tracker advancement.
Timelines retain the original mainly European selection. Corrected period headings and explicit antecedent labels preserve figure order; this is not a global history.
The second glossary preserves thirty original entries including overlapping paired contrasts. These are entries, not a claim to thirty mutually exclusive concepts.
Current-interest lists are framed relative to the original 2024 conversation, not as a newly measured 2026 ranking.
Primary research was scoped as recorded; historical interpretation remains selective. No claim that one definition of knowledge or theory of truth is settled.
Browser verification is desktop/mobile quiz-layout spot checking; mobile position used explicit scrolling, not certified mobile anchor arrival. Static quizzes keep end keys.
All prior page-specific concerns and all35 approved site-native baselines remain effective. No new baseline approval requested.
Saved project path remains absent; actual repository is in iCloud Documents. Saved automation model is gpt-6-astra/high; runtime identity not independently verified.

originalPromptTexts: List and define 30 key terms in epistemology.
List and provide explanations of key concepts in epistemology.
Provide a timeline of epistemology. Include deeper explanations for any paradigm shifts.
List and describe new areas of interest in epistemology.
Create a 10-item quiz based on the content above with answers at the end.
Provide 15 discussion questions relevant to the content above on epistemology.
